metrics.unit: network/checkpoint; related windows are not independent trials

limitations: Three independent 112-instrument, seven-segment, 11.2 km recordings of 360 seconds.
Recorded 60-second numerical windows are sampled every 15 source seconds.
Agents run at predeclared 150/360-second checkpoints only when pressure anomalies exist. This evaluates classification/localization, not automatic admission latency.
Source ingestion is frozen during each real investigation; inference wall time and source time are separate. Playback compresses time, not agent computation.
Both checkpoints and failed/withheld outputs count. Adjacent windows share data and are not independent population trials.
The broad-footprint source remains in localization recall even when its interval is withheld. The 400 m maximum interval is unchanged.
Continuous weak physical influence has no binary anomaly ground-truth threshold; numerical flags are displayed, not assigned fabricated precision/recall labels.
Labels and recipes never enter runtime tools or truth-blind output extraction.
Model-based extraction may make semantic errors; exact quotes remain inspectable.
Generated pressure fields are not field-calibrated hydraulic models.

payload.purpose: answer_incident_question
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.

verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

Recommended next step
Prioritize integrity review on pipe P6 around stations ST5 and ST6, with ST4 and ST7 as surrounding review locations: this is the strongest supported joint pressure-loss pattern. Next, examine P7's alternating low-pressure stations through independent pressure and measurement-connection checks, and P2's broad pressure rise through operating checks. These branches need different attention, not dismissal. No individual sensor is established as unreliable.

What the readings show
On P6, both sensors at ST5 and ST6 read about 1.38–1.40 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. Surrounding ST4 and ST7 deficits are about 0.37–0.39 bar, while outer P6 stations show roughly 0.11–0.19 bar deficits. The executed comparison also shows an approximately 1.38–1.39 bar before/after fall at ST5/ST6, developing after 90 seconds elapsed in the recording. Smaller simultaneous falls appear at connected P3 ST7/ST8; distant P5 ST7/ST8 instead rise slightly. This connected contrast supports the review priority, not a confirmed leak.

Why this matters
P7's paired sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 remain roughly 0.75–0.84 bar below typical pressure, versus about 0.003–0.067 bar at every other station. Those deficits persist throughout the reviewed 90–150-second window; their onset is not observed. Small variation within that window does not make them normal. This separated pattern needs independent checks before attributing it to a physical pressure distribution or shared measurement bias. P2's paired readings across ST1–ST8 rise about 0.38–0.42 bar above typical pressure, warranting operating verification rather than the same localized-loss interpretation. No operating records were supplied or matched.

Other instruments to check
P6 screening flags occur on P6-ST1-A, P6-ST2-B, P6-ST3-A/B, P6-ST7-B and P6-ST8-A/B, but reviewed profiles show coherent pressure changes, not demonstrated isolated instrument spikes. Reviewed health reports show no missing or invalid readings, gradual drift or paired disagreement. Overall sample coverage is 100%, but the health review is partial: completeness does not prove every instrument's accuracy.

What would resolve the remaining question
Ask an engineer to verify independent pressure and flow evidence, executed valve/compressor changes, and shared data or calibration paths. The P6 pattern crosses two reported gateways—the sensors' shared data connections—but their independence still needs register verification. A qualified inspection interval remains withheld: sustained screening support is observed for only 54–59 seconds, and no accepted bounding interval is available. ST5/ST6 is a station-level review focus, not a guessed leak point.

Surrounding P6 stations and connected P3 locations show weaker falls, whereas distant P5 comparisons rise slightly. These observations support integrity review, but an operating transient or shared measurement bias remains unexcluded. Independent pressure and flow verification would help distinguish physical pressure loss from those alternatives. answer.text:
Recommended next step
Prioritize integrity review on pipe P6 around stations ST5 and ST6, with ST4 and ST7 as surrounding comparison locations: this is the strongest supported joint pressure-loss pattern. Next, check P7's contrasting station readings against independent pressure references and measurement connections, and check P2's broad pressure rise against executed operating changes. A leak remains a possible explanation for P6; no individual sensor is established as unreliable.

What the readings show
P6-ST5-A and P6-ST6-A read about 1.40 and 1.38 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. P6-ST4-A and P6-ST7-A have smaller deficits, about 0.38 and 0.39 bar. Separately, the completed before/after comparison shows both sensors at each central station falling together by approximately 1.38–1.39 bar after 90 seconds elapsed in the recording. These paired sensors are two sensors at the same station. Surrounding ST4/ST7 falls are about 0.35–0.39 bar, and outer P6 falls about 0.11–0.19 bar. These changes compare earlier and later readings, not typical-pressure references. Connected P3 ST7/ST8 show smaller falls; distant P5 ST7/ST8 rise slightly.

Why this matters
On P7, reviewed A sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 show deficits of about 0.76–0.84 bar from typical pressure, compared with about 0.064 bar at P7-ST2-A. Their below-reference condition persists throughout the reviewed 90–150-second period; its onset is not observed. Small variation does not erase that deficit. On P2, P2-ST1-A, P2-ST5-B and P2-ST8-B show approximately 0.38–0.42 bar increases above typical pressure, with screening rise periods from 90 to 145 seconds. This opposite sign warrants a separate operating check. No valve/compressor records were supplied.

Other instruments to check
Health reports for P6-ST5-A and P6-ST6-A show no missing or excluded readings, suspected drift, or disagreement with their partners. Compared P6 profiles show coherent pressure changes; screening flags alone do not establish unreliable sensors. Overall sample coverage is 100%, but health review is partial: completeness does not establish each instrument's accuracy, consistent with KN-QUALITY-R1. P7's spatial contrast warrants verification, not a faulty-sensor label.

What would resolve the remaining question
An engineer should verify independent pressure and flow measurements, executed operating changes, and shared calibration or data paths. P6's central pattern spans two reported gateways, meaning shared data connections; their independence needs instrumentation-register verification. No qualified inspection interval was accepted, and the reviewed evidence does not establish the reason for withholding it. ST5/ST6 is therefore a station-level review focus, not a bounded inspection interval or a guessed leak point.

competing_causes.text: P6 provides the strongest leak-pattern evidence: the reviewed A sensors at ST5/ST6 have approximately 1.38–1.40 bar deficits from typical pressure, and the completed comparison shows large synchronized falls on both sensors at those stations. Surrounding P6 stations and connected P3 locations show weaker falls, whereas distant P5 comparisons rise slightly. These observations support integrity review, but an operating transient or shared measurement bias remains unexcluded. Independent pressure and flow verification would help distinguish physical pressure loss from those alternatives. The checked suspected-leak label is numerical screening, and the station-level priority is neither a qualified inspection interval nor a confirmed leak location.

P2-ST1-A, P2-ST5-B and P2-ST8-B show approximately 0.38–0.42 bar increases above typical pressure, with reviewed screening rise periods from 90 to 145 seconds elapsed in the recording. These separated instruments justify checking operating changes without attributing their readings to a confirmed process cause. No valve/compressor records were supplied, so the pressure pattern has not been tested against those operating records. A positive shift on P2 does not by itself explain P6's concentrated negative pattern or P7's contrasting station deficits. An engineer should compare executed valve, compressor and pressure-setting records with each branch's sign and timing separately, as advised by KN-OPERATING-R1.

P7-ST1-A, P7-ST3-A, P7-ST5-A and P7-ST7-A show approximately 0.76–0.84 bar deficits from typical pressure throughout the reviewed period, while P7-ST2-A has a much smaller deficit of about 0.064 bar. The completed comparison contains no P7 instruments, so it does not establish synchronized P7 profiles or a shared connection dependency. Applying KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, the spatial contrast is a reason to test common measurement causes, not proof that these sensors are faulty. Independent reference readings would help distinguish an actual pressure distribution from a shared measurement bias; partial health review prevents an exhaustive reliability judgment.

The completed comparison shows approximately 0.05–0.09 bar before/after falls on both sensors at connected P3 stations ST7/ST8, while both sensors at distant P5 stations ST7/ST8 rise about 0.02–0.04 bar. sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.

Recommended next step
Prioritize integrity review on pipe P6 around stations ST5 and ST6, with ST4 and ST7 as surrounding comparison locations: this is the strongest supported joint pressure-loss pattern. Next, check P7's contrasting station readings against independent pressure references and measurement connections, and check P2's broad pressure rise against executed operating changes. A leak remains a possible explanation for P6; no individual sensor is established as unreliable.

What the readings show
P6-ST5-A and P6-ST6-A read about 1.40 and 1.38 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. P6-ST4-A and P6-ST7-A have smaller deficits, about 0.38 and 0.39 bar. Separately, the completed before/after comparison shows both sensors at each central station falling together by approximately 1.38–1.39 bar after 90 seconds elapsed in the recording. These paired sensors are two sensors at the same station. Surrounding ST4/ST7 falls are about 0.35–0.39 bar, and outer P6 falls about 0.11–0.19 bar. These changes compare earlier and later readings, not typical-pressure references. Connected P3 ST7/ST8 show smaller falls; distant P5 ST7/ST8 rise slightly.

Why this matters
On P7, reviewed A sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 show deficits of about 0.76–0.84 bar from typical pressure, compared with about 0.064 bar at P7-ST2-A. Their below-reference condition persists throughout the reviewed 90–150-second period; its onset is not observed. Small variation does not erase that deficit. On P2, P2-ST1-A, P2-ST5-B and P2-ST8-B show approximately 0.38–0.42 bar increases above typical pressure, with screening rise periods from 90 to 145 seconds. This opposite sign warrants a separate operating check. No valve/compressor records were supplied.

Other instruments to check
Health reports for P6-ST5-A and P6-ST6-A show no missing or excluded readings, suspected drift, or disagreement with their partners. Compared P6 profiles show coherent pressure changes; screening flags alone do not establish unreliable sensors. Overall sample coverage is 100%, but health review is partial: completeness does not establish each instrument's accuracy, consistent with KN-QUALITY-R1. P7's spatial contrast warrants verification, not a faulty-sensor label.

What would resolve the remaining question
An engineer should verify independent pressure and flow measurements, executed operating changes, and shared calibration or data paths. P6's central pattern spans two reported gateways, meaning shared data connections; their independence needs instrumentation-register verification. No qualified inspection interval was accepted, and the reviewed evidence does not establish the reason for withholding it. ST5/ST6 is therefore a station-level review focus, not a bounded inspection interval or a guessed leak point.

Surrounding P6 stations and connected P3 locations show weaker falls, whereas distant P5 comparisons rise slightly. These observations support integrity review, but an operating transient or shared measurement bias remains unexcluded. Independent pressure and flow verification would help distinguish physical pressure loss from those alternatives. cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.

cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.
