payload.text:
Recommended next step
Prioritize integrity-engineer review of pipeline P6 around stations ST5 and ST6, with ST4 and ST7 as surrounding context: this is the strongest supported joint low-pressure pattern, not an identified leak point. Second, review P7's separate alternating-station pressure pattern against operating and measurement arrangements. In parallel, check the specific inconsistent instruments below. A leak remains a possible explanation for P6; instrumentation issues elsewhere do not explain it away. The numerical screening finding is suspected_leak, not a confirmed physical cause (claim-113; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1).

What the readings show
At P6-ST5-A/B and P6-ST6-A/B, the two sensors at each station agree on pressures approximately 1.43-1.46 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. Deficits are about 0.40-0.41 bar at ST4/ST7 and 0.21 bar at ST3/ST8. The central deficit is therefore roughly seven times the ST3/ST8 deficit. It persists through elapsed seconds 300-360 of the recording. The completed comparison covering seconds 240-360 found only 0.004-0.031 bar further decreases at ST5/ST6 across its 300-second split: pressure was already low before that split, so onset was not observed there. P4/P5 station ST6 remained close to their normal references (ev-170 through ev-192; comparison subsea_9f1313bb88ae43e1abcdd8e00d56e6ef).

Why this matters
P6 supports a focused review despite small within-window changes; steady pressure below normal is not normal pressure. P7 also needs attention: paired sensors at ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 show approximately 0.76-0.86 bar deficits, versus 0.01-0.11 bar at the intervening stations. That separated pattern warrants different checks rather than dismissal. A qualified inspection interval is withheld: available summaries do not establish clean unaffected bounding stations, and P7 contains separate affected groups. Use P6-ST5/ST6 as a station-level review focus, not a guessed inspection boundary (ev-194 through ev-224; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1).

Other instruments to check
P1-ST6-A shows upward drift and disagreement with its stable partner P1-ST6-B; P3-ST7-A shows downward drift and disagreement with P3-ST7-B. P2-ST3-A and P4-ST7-B each have two brief screening spikes; P3-ST7-B has one screening excursion, not established unreliability. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings; P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid, excluded readings. P5-ST8-B is flatlined, with zero recorded pressure range. These are suspect observations, not confirmed hardware faults. P6's spike flags alone do not establish unreliable sensors. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial (claims-010/013/020/041/044/045/061/062/112; ev-160; KN-QUALITY-R1).

What would resolve the remaining question
The agents already compared P6 with nearby stations and P4/P5 references; no operating records were supplied or reviewed. Request independent pressure and flow verification, incident-time operating records, and confirmation of shared data connections to distinguish physical pressure changes from common measurement errors (KN-OPERATING-R1).

The comparison establishes complete coverage and small before/after changes, not P4/P5 departures from normal. Its medians cannot establish normal-reference deficits at all claimed P6 stations using this entry's references. Distinguish pre-split change from baseline deficit.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.

cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.

A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.

Recommended next step
First, focus the integrity engineer's evidence review on pipe P7 at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, where both sensors at each station show the strongest sustained pressure deficits. Pair that review with verification of their shared data connection. Second, review operating conditions on P2, which shows a broad pressure rise and late recovery. Separately, check the specific inconsistent measurement paths listed below. These are distinct attention tracks, not a confirmed leak or a choice between mutually exclusive causes.

What the readings show
On P7, sensors P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B read approximately 0.72-0.74 bar below their normal reference; bar is a pressure unit. The deficit persists throughout the reviewed 90-150 seconds of elapsed recording time. Nearby ST2, ST4, ST6 and ST8 remain within approximately 0.04 bar of their references. The executed comparison finds only small before/after changes at the deficient stations, about +0.008 to +0.046 bar across the 120-second split. That means the low readings were already present, not that pressure was normal; their onset was not observed.

Why this matters
Every other P7 station with the deficit shares gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; the quieter stations use gateway-P7-1. Agreement between paired sensors therefore does not supply independent confirmation. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent observation coverage is inadequate. The station-level focus remains useful, but it is not a continuous inspection bracket or a leak point. On P2, all station summaries show roughly 0.40-0.43 bar above normal during the recent 130-150-second period. Compared stations change together, then fall about 0.36-0.41 bar relative to their earlier levels during 146-150 seconds, supporting a separate process check rather than dismissal as faulty sensors.

Other instruments to check
P1-ST6-A shows upward drift and paired disagreement; P3-ST7-A shows downward drift and paired disagreement. Their B partners remain near their normal references. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spike flags with one-second persistence. P6-ST8-B is completely unchanging, a suspect flatline. P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid, excluded readings; P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings. These are observed reading problems, not confirmed hardware faults. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial and that aggregate does not establish local accuracy.

What would resolve the remaining question
The agents already compared P7 and P2 profiles and connection assignments; no operating documents were read. Request independent pressure and flow verification for P7, confirmation of gateway and calibration dependencies, and incident-time operating records for P2. KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-QUALITY-R1 and KN-OPERATING-R1 guide these distinctions but do not establish a physical cause.

COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
leak (possible): P7's normal-reference deficits warrant integrity review: representative readings at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 are approximately 0.72–0.74 bar below normal throughout the reviewed period. Their comparison shows small positive within-window changes, rather than a newly developing joint decline. All paired measurement paths at these stations share one gateway, so their agreement cannot independently establish a physical pressure loss. KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1 therefore supports retaining a leak hypothesis while testing shared measurement effects. Independent pressure and flow observations would help distinguish the alternatives; the present evidence cannot qualify an inspection interval.

answer.text:
Recommended next step
First, focus integrity review on pipeline P7 at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, alongside verification of their shared measurement connection. Their sustained below-normal readings are the strongest supported pressure-deficit pattern. This is a station-level review priority, not a qualified inspection section. Second, check P2 operating conditions for its broad pressure elevation and coordinated late fall. Separately, verify the questionable instruments identified below. A leak remains possible; shared measurement bias is an unresolved alternative on P7.

What the readings show
Representative P7 readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST3-B have typical deficits of approximately 0.724 and 0.742 bar relative to normal; bar is a pressure unit. Their below-normal periods extend from 90 to 150 seconds of elapsed recording time. Nearby P7-ST2-A is approximately 0.037 bar above normal. The executed comparison shows both sensors at each of ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 increasing only slightly across the 120-second split, approximately 0.008–0.046 bar. Small within-recording changes do not erase an existing normal-reference deficit; the deficit's onset was not observed.

Why this matters
Those four P7 stations share gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; every other station uses gateway-P7-1. Paired sensors—two sensors at the same station—can agree while sharing a measurement error. Independent observation coverage is inadequate to qualify an inspection interval, so none is supplied. P2 warrants process checks rather than dismissal: P2-ST1-A and P2-ST7-B are approximately 0.392 and 0.426 bar above normal during 130–150 seconds. Eight compared P2 sensors across both listed connections show a coordinated fall of approximately 0.356–0.409 bar during 146–150 seconds relative to their earlier within-recording reference levels. This does not establish an operating cause or isolated sensor faults.

Other instruments to check
P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A show suspected gradual drift and disagreement with their paired sensors. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spike flags with one-second persistence. P6-ST8-B is entirely unchanging, a suspect flatline. P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded invalid readings. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings. These are measurement concerns, not confirmed hardware faults. Usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial; completeness does not establish every instrument's accuracy.

What would resolve the remaining question
The agents already compared P7 and P2 profiles and their listed connection assignments. Request independent P7 pressure and flow verification, confirmation of connection and calibration dependencies, and incident-time operating verification for P2. KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1 and KN-QUALITY-R1 guide these checks without establishing a physical cause.

competing_causes.text: P7's normal-reference deficits warrant integrity review: representative readings at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 are approximately 0.72–0.74 bar below normal throughout the reviewed period. Their comparison shows small positive within-window changes, rather than a newly developing joint decline. All paired measurement paths at these stations share one gateway, so their agreement cannot independently establish a physical pressure loss. KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1 therefore supports retaining a leak hypothesis while testing shared measurement effects. Independent pressure and flow observations would help distinguish the alternatives; the present evidence cannot qualify an inspection interval.

The compared P7 station groups use different gateways, making a shared measurement-path explanation worth checking without labelling every sensor on gateway-P7-0 faulty. Concrete reasons for separate instrument checks include suspected drift and paired disagreement at P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A, and the entirely unchanging P6-ST8-B record. These patterns do not confirm a hardware cause and do not exclude a simultaneous physical event. KN-QUALITY-R1 calls for independent references before attributing inaccurate readings to equipment. Verify pressure independently and compare the actual connection and calibration dependencies with the observed patterns.

P2-ST1-A and P2-ST7-B show typical pressures approximately 0.392 and 0.426 bar above normal during 130–150 seconds of elapsed recording time. The eight compared P2 instruments vary together across both listed gateways and show a coordinated late fall, supporting investigation of a common process change rather than isolated measurement impulses. Association alone does not establish an executed operation as the explanation. Verification of a P2 operating transition would not automatically explain P7's separate deficit pattern.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.

What the readings show
Representative P7 readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST3-B have typical deficits of approximately 0.724 and 0.742 bar relative to normal; bar is a pressure unit. Those four P7 stations share gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; every other station uses gateway-P7-1. cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.

cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.

verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. payload.text:
Recommended next step
Focus the integrity engineer's first review on pipe P7 at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, beginning with independent pressure verification and their shared data connection. These locations have the strongest repeated joint pressure deficit, but its every-other-station pattern follows gateway-P7-0, making a common measurement-path check especially important. Separately, review the isolated rising reading on P1 and falling reading on P3 through instrument checks and operating-context verification; neither branch should be ignored or treated as a jointly measured leak pattern.

What the readings show
Both sensors at each affected P7 station report typical pressure about 0.73-0.76 bar below their normal reference; bar is a pressure unit. Nearby ST2, ST4, ST6 and ST8 are approximately 0.006-0.024 bar above their own references. The specialist already compared all P7 stations with P5-ST1-A/B over elapsed seconds 240-360 of the recording. Changes across the 300-second split were small: affected P7 readings decreased only 0.003-0.036 bar. Thus, the deficit was already present before that split; these measurements do not establish its onset or a new pressure drop then.

Why this matters
The paired deficits deserve integrity attention, but eight agreeing sensors on one gateway are not eight independent witnesses. A gateway is their shared data connection. The contrasting stations use gateway-P7-1, and the comparison does not show strongly synchronized pressure fluctuations. Following KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, check the common path without declaring its sensors faulty. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent corroboration is inadequate; the named stations are a review focus, not a leak location.

Other instruments to check
P1-ST6-A shows suspected upward drift and disagreement with its stable paired sensor; P3-ST7-A shows suspected downward drift with a stable paired sensor. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spike flags. P6-ST8-B is an observed flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid/excluded readings; P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings. These are questionable observations, not confirmed hardware faults. Aggregate coverage is 99.18%, but the health review is partial and does not certify every instrument.

What would resolve the remaining question
Request independent pressure and flow verification at the P7 focus stations and confirmation of gateway assignments against the instrumentation register. No operating documents were reviewed: incident-time valve, compressor and pressure-setting records could distinguish process changes from measurement-path effects. KN-QUALITY-R1 and KN-LOCALIZATION-R1 support these checks, not a confirmed cause or permission to operate.

The persistent deficits and small comparison-window changes justify independent verification, not a confirmed leak, onset or location. Shared-gateway and alternating-station qualifications are retained.

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.public_output:
ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Recommended next step
Focus the integrity engineer's first review on pipe P7 at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, where paired sensors show the strongest repeated pressure pattern reviewed. Request independent pressure verification before selecting a physical inspection section. Next, prioritize measurement-path checks for P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A because each disagrees with its paired reference. Keep operating-context checks separate: the isolated P1 rise does not establish a broad process change or explain P7.

What the readings show
P7-ST1-A, P7-ST3-A, P7-ST5-A and P7-ST7-A report typical pressure about 0.73-0.76 bar below their respective normal references; bar is a pressure unit. In contrast, P7-ST2-A is about 0.008 bar above its reference. These numerical deficits describe the named A sensors, not assumed baseline differences for their partners. The specialist already compared all P7 stations with P5-ST1-A/B over elapsed seconds 240-360 of the recording. Across the split at 300 seconds, the affected P7 pairs decreased only 0.003-0.036 bar. Those small within-record changes do not erase the normal-reference deficits or establish when they began.

Why this matters
Both sensors at each affected P7 station share gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; every other P7 station uses gateway-P7-1. Agreement in pressure levels therefore lacks independent connection coverage, while the comparison shows only weakly related fluctuations. A common measurement-path explanation needs verification, not a faulty-sensor declaration. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent corroboration is inadequate. The named stations are a review focus, not a localized leak section; a physical leak remains unestablished.

Other instruments to check
P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A have suspected drift and paired disagreement; P1-ST6-B and P3-ST7-B remain near their normal references. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spike flags requiring review, not proven unreliable sensors. P6-ST8-B is a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded readings; P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings. These findings identify questionable observations, not confirmed hardware faults. Aggregate coverage is 99.18%, but the health review is partial and cannot establish every sensor's reliability.

What would resolve the remaining question
Request independent pressure and flow verification at the P7 focus stations and confirmation of gateway assignments against the instrumentation register. Incident-time valve, compressor and pressure-setting records remain needed to test operating explanations. Applying KN-QUALITY-R1, compare suspect measurement paths with independent references rather than treating an anomaly as a hardware diagnosis; the available pressure comparison need not be repeated.
Sources: subsea_9434c1bf26604e30ba10c8afb2a2eb7f, ev-194, ev-202, ev-210, ev-218, ev-198, claim-010, claim-044, ev-024, ev-092, claim-061, claim-084, ev-192, claim-062, claim-013, claim-041, claim-112, KN-QUALITY-R1
COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
leak (not established): P7-ST1-A, P7-ST5-A and P7-ST7-A have typical pressure about 0.73-0.75 bar below their own normal references, supporting an integrity verification priority. The comparison shows similar paired pressure levels at these stations, but all affected pairs share gateway-P7-0 and alternate with stations on another connection. Only small before/after changes were observed, rather than a new onset at the recording split. Applying KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1 and KN-LOCALIZATION-R1, independent pressure and flow verification is needed before attributing a physical leak or defining an inspection interval.
Sources: ev-194, ev-210, ev-218, subsea_9434c1bf26604e30ba10c8afb2a2eb7f, KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1
instrumentation or telemetry (possible): P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A have suspected drift and disagreement with the other sensor at their respective stations. Their paired-reference summaries show P1-ST6-B and P3-ST7-B close to normal, supporting checks of the A measurement paths rather than labelling both sensors unreliable. Separately, the executed P7 comparison identifies a connection-aligned alternating pressure pattern, making a shared measurement-path explanation worth testing without establishing a connection fault. Applying KN-QUALITY-R1, independent pressure references and engineer review of instrument and connection records would distinguish questionable readings from physical pressure differences.
Sources: claim-010, claim-044, ev-024, ev-092, subsea_9434c1bf26604e30ba10c8afb2a2eb7f, KN-QUALITY-R1
operating change (not testable): P1-ST6-A reads about 3.36 bar above its normal reference while P1-ST6-B is only about 0.011 bar above its own reference. This disagreement weighs against a jointly measured broad rise at that station. P3-ST7-A reads about 3.37 bar below normal while P3-ST7-B remains close to its reference, providing a different isolated pattern. Operating records were not available in the reviewed context, so an executed operating explanation cannot be tested here. Following KN-OPERATING-R1, incident-time records and independent pressure verification are needed; an explanation for one branch must not automatically be applied to P7 or the other branch.
Sources: ev-022, ev-024, ev-090, ev-092, claim-116, KN-OPERATING-R1
Joint sensor assessment (instrumentation or telemetry): P7-ST1-A, P7-ST1-B, P7-ST2-A, P7-ST2-B, P7-ST3-A, P7-ST3-B, P7-ST4-A, P7-ST4-B, P7-ST5-A, P7-ST5-B, P7-ST6-A, P7-ST6-B, P7-ST7-A, P7-ST7-B, P7-ST8-A, P7-ST8-B, P5-ST1-A, P5-ST1-B
On pipe P7, P7-ST1-A and P7-ST1-B are respectively about 0.733 and 0.752 bar below their own normal references, while P7-ST3-A is about 0.760 bar below its reference. P7-ST2-A contrasts with these readings at about 0.008 bar above normal; this comparison uses instrument-specific normal references, not absolute pressures at different stations. The executed comparison of all P7 stations and P5-ST1-A/B shows small within-record shifts and places both sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 on gateway-P7-0, whereas every other P7 station uses gateway-P7-1. Following KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, that connection alignment supports testing a shared measurement path without declaring those sensors faulty or treating their agreement as independent leak evidence. Confirm gateway assignments and obtain independent pressure and flow measurements to distinguish a physical pressure difference from a common measurement bias.
Sources: ev-194, ev-196, ev-202, ev-198, subsea_9434c1bf26604e30ba10c8afb2a2eb7f, KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1
QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE WITH THE ENGINEER
Do independent pressure and flow measurements confirm P7's deficits at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 compared with the quieter stations?
Does the instrumentation register confirm the P7 gateway assignments, and do connection or calibration checks explain the alternating pressure pattern?
Do incident-time operating records explain any branch-specific pressure changes without assuming the same cause on P1, P3 and P7?

Recommended next step
Focus the integrity engineer's first review on pipe P7 at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, where paired sensors show the strongest repeated pressure pattern reviewed. Request independent pressure verification before selecting a physical inspection section. Next, prioritize measurement-path checks for P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A because each disagrees with its paired reference. Keep operating-context checks separate: the isolated P1 rise does not establish a broad process change or explain P7.

What the readings show
P7-ST1-A, P7-ST3-A, P7-ST5-A and P7-ST7-A report typical pressure about 0.73-0.76 bar below their respective normal references; bar is a pressure unit. In contrast, P7-ST2-A is about 0.008 bar above its reference. These numerical deficits describe the named A sensors, not assumed baseline differences for their partners. The specialist already compared all P7 stations with P5-ST1-A/B over elapsed seconds 240-360 of the recording. Across the split at 300 seconds, the affected P7 pairs decreased only 0.003-0.036 bar. Those small within-record changes do not erase the normal-reference deficits or establish when they began.

Why this matters
Both sensors at each affected P7 station share gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; every other P7 station uses gateway-P7-1. Agreement in pressure levels therefore lacks independent connection coverage, while the comparison shows only weakly related fluctuations. A common measurement-path explanation needs verification, not a faulty-sensor declaration. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent corroboration is inadequate. The named stations are a review focus, not a localized leak section; a physical leak remains unestablished.

Other instruments to check
P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A have suspected drift and paired disagreement; P1-ST6-B and P3-ST7-B remain near their normal references. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spike flags requiring review, not proven unreliable sensors. P6-ST8-B is a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded readings; P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings. These findings identify questionable observations, not confirmed hardware faults. Aggregate coverage is 99.18%, but the health review is partial and cannot establish every sensor's reliability.

What would resolve the remaining question
Request independent pressure and flow verification at the P7 focus stations and confirmation of gateway assignments against the instrumentation register. Incident-time valve, compressor and pressure-setting records remain needed to test operating explanations. Applying KN-QUALITY-R1, compare suspect measurement paths with independent references rather than treating an anomaly as a hardware diagnosis; the available pressure comparison need not be repeated.
